sections.content:
Looking at the segmentation data, I can see the player (blue, id=27) is at center (28,28). The adjacent objects show:
- id=26 (gray) at center (28,25) - to the left
- id=30 (charcoal) at (28,29) - a single pixel to the right
- id=22 (gray) at center (25,28) - above
- And various other objects
The key insight is that the player is surrounded by gray (g) cells and there's a charcoal (c) pixel at (28,29) which might be blocking movement. Let me look at the adjacency list to understand connectivity.
But more importantly, I notice the player has only 8 pixels (not 9 like other 3x3 blocks). This suggests the player might be a 3x3 block with one pixel different (the 'c' at (28,29)).
Let me think about this differently. The maze seems to have a pattern where:
- White (W) cells are walkable paths
- Gray (g) cells are walls or borders
- Black (B) cells are solid walls
- The player (blue) needs to navigate through white cells
But the player is currently surrounded by gray cells, not white cells. This means the player is in a "dead end" or the wrong path.
Wait, let me reconsider the entire maze structure. Looking at the centers:
- Row centers: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46
- Col centers: 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46
The player is at (28, 28) = grid cell (2, 2). Looking at the objects around:
- (28, 22) = W (id=25) - to the left
- (28, 25) = g (id=26) - between player and left white cell
- (28, 28) = b (player)
- (28, 29) = c (id=30) - single pixel to the right of player
- (28, 34) = W (id=28) - further right
So the player is between gray cells on the left and a charcoal pixel on the right. The charcoal pixel might be a "door" or special cell that needs to be activated.
Actually, I wonder if the charcoal (c) pixel is part of the player or a separate object. Looking at the boundary: [[28, 29]], it's a single pixel. And the player has 8 pixels (not 9), suggesting one pixel of the 3x3 block is charcoal instead of blue.
Let me try a different approach: probe each direction individually to see which ones actually work.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Probe each direction individually
for direction in ['UP', 'DOWN', 'LEFT', 'RIGHT']:
    # Get current player position before probing
    seg_before = current_frame.segmentation
    player_before = None
    for n in seg_before['nodes']:
        if n['color'] == 'b':
            player_before = n
            break
    
    # Execute the move
    result = action([direction])
    
    # Get player position after
    seg_after = current_frame.segmentation
    player_after = None
    for n in seg_after['nodes']:
        if n['color'] == 'b':
            player_after = n
            break
    
    # Check if player moved
    moved = player_before['boundary'] != player_after['boundary']
    print(f"{direction}: moved={moved}, gameplay_changed={result.get('gameplay_changed')}, no_impact={result.get('no_impact')}")
    if moved:
        print(f"  From {player_before['boundary']} to {player_after['boundary']}")
        break  # Stop after finding a working move
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
